subject: Recap + unit-econ action items from today's demo
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Boyd <sarah.boyd@tonalytics.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@tonalytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + unit-econ action items from today's demo

Thanks for carving out time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the unit economics inputs we need to build a concrete pricing recommendation.

Call highlights (TL;DR)
- Feature: contextual feedback assistant embedded in product (per-user, in-app).
- Pilot expectations: 30k UA for 30 days (sandbox), production year-1 ramp to ~300k MAUs.
- Current internal proxy: ~150 tokens/request, average 3 requests/user/day (we'll refine).
- Initial ask from you: target payback / CAC and target $/1M tokens to hit margin goals.

Requested inputs from Tonalytics (action items)
1) Baseline pilot and production token volume estimates (per day / per month) — needed to model unit cost by scenario.
2) Target gross margin on the feature (e.g., 35%–50%).
3) CAC payback target (months).
4) Any hard budget range for cloud/inference spend (monthly) you have for year-1.

What we will deliver (by Tue EOD PST)
- A filled unit-econ workbook with two scenarios (hosted burst + reserved capacity) giving $/1M-token breakouts, $/feature, and CAC payback curves.
- A recommendation: pilot pricing band + production pricing ladder and suggested commitment sizes to hit your margin and payback targets.

Next steps
- Sarah/Tom: reply with the four inputs above (even approximate numbers are fine).
- Redwood: will attach the workbook and a pricing term sheet after we get your numbers, then schedule a short follow-up (30 min) to review.

Attachments: none in this message — I will send the workbook once you confirm the numbers.

Best,
Rafael Mendes

Thanks Rafael — quick answers below so you can start modeling. Apologies for the rough numbers, procurement will tighten them up later.

1) Token volume estimates (initial view)
- Pilot (30 days): 1.2M tokens total (~40k tokens/day) — conservative sandbox.
- Production year-1 (month average): 28M tokens/month (~933k tokens/day) once we reach ~300k MAUs and adoption assumptions hold.
- Peak day assumption for capacity planning: ~1.5M tokens/day.

2) Target gross margin on the feature: 40% (target for product management) — they're flexible but won't accept <30%.

3) CAC payback target: 9 months (ideally 6–9).

4) Budget range: For inference alone we have a starting budget guidance of $8k–$20k/month in year-1 depending on commitments and SLA. Procurement prefers predictable commits if unit economics justify it.

Also: primary KPI for us is $/active feature user per month (we'll need your $/feature calc).

If you need more granular per-request tokens I can pull logs but that'll take 48 hrs.

—Sarah

Subject: Unit-econ workbook attached + preliminary lifts and asks

Appended the workbook and a term sheet (attached) with a couple of preliminary scenarios based on your numbers. Short summary of the modeling assumptions we used (see attached sheet 'assumptions'):
- Token mix: 60% short (30–80 tokens), 40% long (200–400 tokens) => average ~145 tokens/request.
- Requests per active user/day: 3 (you can change this in the workbook).
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go) baseline inference cost used: $1,200 per 1M tokens (no commit).
- Reserved / Dedicated discount ladder: 20% at 1M/day commit, 35% at 3M/day commit (indicative).

Preliminary outputs (rounded) — please treat as directional:
- If you run hosted at $1,200/1M tokens and deliver the feature as in-app with 3 rps/user, $/feature/month = ~$0.52 (at 300k MAUs scenario).
- To hit 40% gross margin and 9-month CAC payback given your LTV/CAC assumptions, your target inference cost needs to be in the ~$700–$900 per 1M tokens band.
- With a 3M/day reserved commit we can push to ~$780/1M tokens (after discounts + minor cache savings).

Questions for you to finalize the workbook
- Confirm average requests/user/day (3 used here).
- Confirm share of long vs short requests (I used 40% long).
- Confirm any internal rate to attribute per-feature revenue (do you price the feature as add-on or include in base plan?).

Attachments: Tonalytics_unit_econ_workbook.xlsx (workbook), redwood-pricing-term-sheet.pdf (term sheet)

If that looks directionally sane I'll prepare 2 pricing options to present to your procurement: 1) short-term hosted pilot pricing band, 2) 12-month reserved commit with aggressive $/1M step-downs. Can we book 30 min Mon to walk the workbook?

Best,
Rafael

Adding a couple of operational notes from Solutions engineering side. Sarah / Tom — copying Rafael but wanted to flag options that commonly move the needle on $/1M tokens: 

- Prefix + KV caching: expect 8–15% token savings if your UI patterns reuse prompts (we can instrument on pilot).
- Model family choice: if you can tolerate a slightly smaller model on tail queries we can reduce per-token compute by ~12% without large quality regressions.
- Pilot offer: 30-day canary with 1M tokens/day cap, full observability export (billing + token-level latency), and a one-off 10% credit on first-month committed dollars for new customers.

I'll attach a short pilot SLA stub (redwood-pilot-sla.pdf) and a checklist for procurement (doc link in this thread). If procurement is aiming for predictable monthly spend, the reserved commit route is almost always cheaper on a per-token basis and gives you more predictable CAC payback math.

Let me know if you want me to model a pilot-with-triggered-commit scenario (pilot triggers a 6/12 month commit if certain KPI thresholds hit).

—Monica
